description: Provenance + regeneration parameters for the painterly tileset (see README.md)
model: gemini-3-pro-image-preview (Nano Banana Pro) via Vertex AI, project hex-general, location global

tile_spec.hex: flat-top, point-to-point width 128 (2x render HEX_SIZE=32; drawn at 64 world px, crisp at MAX_ZOOM=2)
tile_spec.mask: hexgeom.hex_mask(128,128) core >128, dilated 1px (bleed) so abutting tiles overlap real content instead of AA fading

plains.gates: all 49 candidates passed luminance band 100-125 (measured 109-120); picks from a 23-candidate mutually seam-compatible clique (pre-v2 seam metric); truncation 0 fails

woods.class: object field (composited sprites; never swatch-cut - user: no cut-off canopies, trees end before the hex edge)

segmentation.connected_components: 8-neighbour, min area 400 px (prompt asked 6x6 grid but got 7 columns; components make the layout irrelevant)

compose.edge_inset: centre of crown must satisfy in_hex with shrink 2 + 0.72*max(w,h)/2 (no tree crosses the true hex edge)
compose.draw_order: sorted by y_base ascending (lower trees composite over higher)
compose.floor_discs: per tree, r=0.72*w at crown centre, rgba(30,44,26,185), gaussian blur 2, clipped to dilated mask
compose.placements: woods/placements.json (exact per-tree x, y_base, size, sprite index)

woods.ratified: 2026-07-01 via woods/review/woods-final-*.png ('sprites and layout are great' + packed density per 'can't really see much of the ground')

hills.class: whole-hex vignette (composited hill formations via vignette.py; swatch-cut texture REJECTED 2026-07-01: relief contrast breaks seams - best swatch's largest seam-compatible clique was 2/49 cuts vs plains' 23, and flatten.py can't help because the contrast IS the ridges, not illumination)

segmentation.foreground: min-channel distance from white > 25, alpha ramp (dist-25)*255/60
segmentation.discovery: downsample 8x (block max), hole-fill via border-connected background components, 4 largest clusters, row-major order
segmentation.interior: forced opaque (erode 2 at low res) so bright rock never goes transparent
segmentation.unmatte: partial-alpha edge pixels un-matted from white (kills the halo)

grass_match.note: recolour option 'a' ratified from hills/review/hills-recolor-compare.png (columns: original|a|b|c); grass-weighted so rocky crests stay put; also drops whitish low-sat pixels near the alpha boundary (the 'whitish seam' the user flagged)

hills.ratified: 2026-07-01 ('Hills A'), applied tiles also archived at hills/picks/

city.class: settlement vignette (whole-hex composition on a grass rim via vignette.py)
style_refs: city/street-guide.png (layout diagram, NOT style: 6 streets to the flat-top hex edge midpoints at 30/90/150/210/270/330 deg, where roads will enter later)
city.segmentation: same recipe as hills.segmentation, no grass_match (city needs no recolour)
city.vignette_history: v1 organic (no spoke control) -> v2 six spokes but a perfect wheel with boulevard streets -> v3 ratified: six narrow lanes in the diagram directions, ragged organic outline
city.ratified: 2026-07-01 ('cities are good'), applied tiles also archived at city/picks/

town.class: settlement vignette (whole-hex composition on a grass rim via vignette.py; the smaller sibling of city)
style_refs: refs/town_a.png (concept1.png crop (950,240)-(1115,365), the small village at the road junction)
city/street-guide.png (layout diagram, NOT style: same 6 lane directions as city so roads can anchor at the flat-top hex edge midpoints later)
town.segmentation: same recipe as hills.segmentation, no grass_match (like city, town needs no recolour)
town.sheet_history: sheet 1 rejected (cluster 4 was a smeared generation failure; its 3 good clusters read more rural/sparse - offered as row town_b and not picked); sheet 2 ratified whole (all 4 clusters clean, denser small-town register)
town.ratified: 2026-07-01 ('Town a sounds fine', feature_px 80 vs the town_a90 size alternative; city-tile reference row in town/review/town-a-candidates.png), applied tiles also archived at town/picks/

river.class: oriented texture (swatch-cut straight_v + straight_d + the four gentle-turn shapes + the fork_se_sw_s tributary junction; remaining fork orientations, ends and bridge still legacy PixelLab — later slices per ART_PIPELINE decision 4). Render-time L↔R mirror covers the other diagonal/turn orientations (see frontend riverTiles.ts, which also prunes junction-triangle adjacency artifacts so only the true junction hex renders a fork).
river.prompt: river/river-prompt-v7.txt (v4-v6 history: v4 good register but sandbars + curved edge entries; v7 bans sandbars outright and demands the course track the band's straights exactly)
style_refs: refs/ref_river_concept.png (creek register: narrow grey-teal water, concept-art crop)

layout_guide.note: node-straightened meander (river.py guide): straight vertical plateaus at every tile-period node, one sin^2 out-and-back lobe between - bends finish before the flat edges, so tiled columns never jerk at seams (user requirement 2026-07-02). Constant band width: a mid-lobe bulge in earlier guides invited per-bend sandbars.

river.generation_variance: NBP band-following is ~50/50 with no seed control; 3 of 6 rolls painted 150-250px braided rivers instead. Re-roll on failure; this swatch was roll 2 of the v7 prompt.

cut.note: 3:1 multi-scale cut (384px window LANCZOS-downscaled to the 128px tile) is the width control: the model overshoots the band ~1.5x, so cutting at 3x brings the water to 13-15 tile px. Side effect: river grass grain is finer than the 1:1-cut plains.

river.gates: river.py cut, tile px: crossing centre off <=3, top/bottom centre mismatch <=2, width mismatch <=4, width band 12-36, drift <=26, water half-span <=31, edge-straight dev <=2.5 over 18px spans; picks measured ct/cb <=0.9, water 13-15px, es <=1.8

recolor.note: hills-style grass-weighted HSV match toward the plains grass-core medians (recomputed from plains/picks, not hardcoded), with the sat ramp raised from hills' 0.12 so the desaturated water (sat ~0.21, hue ~90 - inside the hills weight!) keeps its ratified colour. Dropped worst angled seam 3.36->2.15 and dc step 15.8->6.9-9.4.

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v8-zzv.txt (v7 base reworded for a zigzagging course: crisp 60° corners, straight legs between)
sources.generation_variance: NBP smooths the crisp zigzag into meanders more often than not (rolls 1 and 3 unusable); this swatch was roll 2, whose painted corners sat close enough to the guide's for the ±300px window search to find them.

cut.note: 6.75:1 multi-scale cut: the zigzag swatches over-painted the band ~2.4x (vs straight_v's ~1.5x), so the wider window brings the water back to the shipped 14-16 tile px. Corner geometry is scale-free (both legs' lines pass through the corner point), so only the window size changes.

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v8-zzh.txt (zzv prompt with the course running between the left and right edges)
sources.generation_variance: roll 1 followed the band; corners within the ±200px search.

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v8-diag.txt (single dead-straight 30° course; the zigzag swatches' diagonal legs always curved, so straight_d got its own guide)
sources.generation_variance: roll 1 followed the band exactly; cleanest of the v8 swatches (3 of 4 gate-passing cuts under the 2.0 seam gate post-recolor, matching the shipped straight_v range).

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v9-fork.txt (v8-zzh reworded for two straight S tributaries leaving the zigzag peaks; bans junction pools/ponds/islands/deltas outright — the fork-specific failure mode)
sources.generation_variance: roll 1 followed the band cleanly at both junctions — no braiding, no delta, width overshoot only ~1.3x (vs the zigzags' ~2.4x), hence the smaller 512px cut window.

cut.note: 4:1 multi-scale cut: this swatch tracked the 40px band much closer than the zigzag swatches, so 512px (not 864) lands the water at the shipped 14-18 tile px. Post-recolor grass seams 2.65/3.23 — the ratified turn range (user ratified 2026-07-02, w512 pair).

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v10-branch-v.txt (vertical creek with a single straight 60° tributary joining each junction; v9-fork base, same junction-pool/pond/island/delta bans)
sources.generation_variance: r1 ignored the band (width blowout ~4.2x, unusable); r2 tracked both junctions cleanly but painted wide — core ~126px, ~3.1x overshoot vs the 40px band.

cut.note: 7.5:1 primary cut for the ~3.1x overshoot — brings the water back to the shipped 14-18 tile px. The 864 cut of the same r2 swatch supplies the _01 variants.

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v10-branch-v.txt (vertical creek with a single straight 60° tributary joining each junction; v9-fork base, same junction-pool/pond/island/delta bans)
sources.generation_variance: r1 ignored the band (width blowout ~4.2x, unusable); r2 tracked both junctions cleanly but painted wide — core ~126px, ~3.1x overshoot vs the 40px band.

cut.note: 6.75:1 second cut of the branch-v r2 swatch (a tighter window over the same junctions) for the _01 variants.

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v10-branch-d1.txt (dead-straight 30° course with a 60° tributary off each junction; v9-fork base on the v8-diag course description)
sources.generation_variance: roll 1 followed the band at both junctions; painted core ~75px, ~1.9x overshoot vs the 40px band.

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v10-branch-d2.txt (same 30° course, the other pair of tributary orientations off each junction)
sources.generation_variance: roll 1 followed the band — tightest follow of the fork set: painted core ~50px, only ~1.26x overshoot vs the 40px band.

cut.note: 3.5:1 primary cut for the ~1.26x overshoot. The 384 cut of the same r1 swatch supplies fork_se_nw_sw_01.

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v10-branch-d2.txt (same 30° course, the other pair of tributary orientations off each junction)
sources.generation_variance: roll 1 followed the band — tightest follow of the fork set: painted core ~50px, only ~1.26x overshoot vs the 40px band.

cut.note: 3:1 second cut of the branch-d2 r1 swatch for the fork_se_nw_sw_01 variant; post-recolor grass seam 3.32, at the ratified turn/fork range edge (user accepted).

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v10-y.txt (connected double-Y: two symmetric 120° Y junctions sharing a short connector; v9-fork base)
sources.generation_variance: roll 1 followed the band; painted core ~78px, ~1.95x overshoot vs the 40px band.

cut.note: 5:1 cut for the ~1.95x overshoot. Both 120° Y shapes are self-mirror-symmetric, so each window is its own applied tile.

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v10b-fans-b.txt (v10b = flat-map disclaimer + explicit per-arm compass walk; the plain v10 prompt on r1 replaced the SE arm with a W arm and blew the width ~3.6x)
sources.generation_variance: r1 (v10 prompt) mis-drew the fan — swapped the SE arm for a W arm, width ~3.6x, unusable; r2 (v10b prompt) followed perfectly, painted core ~107px, ~2.7x overshoot vs the 40px band.

sources.prompt: river/river-prompt-v11b-ends.txt (v11b = the v10b pattern reworded for four independent spring heads: each stream winds into a very thin trickle that peters out just past the hex centre, explicit no-arrowhead/no-triangular-point language; drives the guide's tapered `ends` kind)
sources.generation_variance: The v11 round painted wedge/arrow-shaped heads; superseded by user direction (2026-07-03) to a snaking, concavely-thinning trickle (guide re-rendered, T_TERMINUS_MAX loosened 0.20→0.30). v11b roll 1 then followed the band at ~0.93–0.95x — the lowest overshoot in the river series (historical 0.93x–3.1x) — with no dead-end pathologies across both rounds (0 re-rolls). A single 352px window cut all four spring heads.

cut.note: 2.75:1 cut for the ~0.93–0.95x band-follow. Edge widths ride the bottom of the 12-tile-px width band when NBP obeys the band exactly, so windows below ~320 or above ~380 fail the floor at this follow; the w320 alternates also passed but the w352 set was ratified (spring nearest the hex centre, airier read). End caps have no water-self pairing; post-recolor grass seams 2.58–3.04, within the ratified fork/turn range.

river.shape_gates: river.py cut --shape, tile px (auto-scaled by window): per-edge crossing centre off <=3, width band 12-36, width mismatch <=4, edge-straight dev <=2.5, opposite-edge centre mismatch <=2 (straights only), hex-boundary ring water only within half-span 31 of connected edge midpoints; picks measured crossings <=0.1, water 14-16px
river.regenerate: python3 scripts/tile-foundry/river.py build --manifest art/foundry/manifest.json --section river --out-dir <dir> [--verify frontend/src/board/tiles/river]
river.ratified: straight_v 2026-07-02 via river/review/creek-v7-recolor-compare.png + creek-v7-recolor-mixcol-*.png ('Nice, looks good'); straight_d + turns 2026-07-02 via montages river-simple-shapes.png + river-course-preview.png ('Looks good... OK taking more than one and using them as variants' — all seam-clean candidates applied); forks (families A/B/C) 2026-07-03 via the fork-candidate montages ('Not bad! ... fine with having multiples of any given shape' — all seam-clean candidates applied as variants): 9 fork shapes / 12 tiles, post-recolor grass seams 2.25-3.32. Parked: the fans-a pair (fork_se_ne_n, fork_ne_n_nw) — 5 rolls, NBP always paints a downstream outlet through the dead-end fan junction (all-arms-upward junctions are hydrologically outlet-free), so it needs a guide redesign if ever wanted. Applied tiles archived at river/picks/
